03

Buyer Details component tree

The busiest screen is split by responsibility. Repeated copy rows become one reusable component.

Component hierarchy

  • BuyerDetailsPage container / fetched record
    • AppHeader organism
    • BuyerSummary organism
      • ActionButton atom
    • ContactDetails organism
      • CopyField × 2 molecule
        • FieldLabel atom
        • CopyButton atom
    • ShippingDetails organism / UI selection
      • ShippingMethodControl molecule
      • SavedLocationSelector molecule
      • CopyField × n molecule
      • CopyFeedback atom
    • LocationDialog organism
      • FormField × n molecule
      • ButtonGroup molecule

Atomic levels

AtomsButton, Input, Label, Tag, CopyFeedback
MoleculesCopyField, FormField, MethodControl, LocationSelector
OrganismsAppHeader, BuyerSummary, ContactDetails, ShippingDetails, LocationDialog
TemplateDispatchRecordLayout
PageBuyerDetailsPage
State ownership
BuyerDetailsPage owns buyer, addresses, pickups, loading and errors. ShippingDetails owns the selected method/location. CopyField owns short-lived copy feedback. Data moves down; callbacks move changes up.
04

Primary task walkthrough

Sanity check for the manager’s most important job: find a repeat buyer and transfer the correct shipping details.

Find buyer → copy courier-ready details

1. SearchEnter a partial name or phone number in Buyer Directory.
2. OpenChoose the matching buyer from the result list.
3. Choose methodSelect Door to Door or LBC Branch Pickup.
4. Choose locationConfirm the saved default or select another record.
5. CopyCopy one field, the full address, or all shipping details.
6. ConfirmSee text feedback, then paste into the courier form.
✓ No dead endsEvery route returns to Directory or Details.
✓ State has an ownerFetched records, UI selection, and copy feedback are separated.
✓ Phone reflow plannedGrids become a task-ordered stack without horizontal scroll.
